stem: A client is receiving intravenous ferumoxytol for iron-deficiency anemia. Which safety measure is required by the current product label?

options.A: Administer as an IV infusion over at least 15 minutes with anaphylaxis treatment immediately available, and observe during and for at least 30 minutes afterward.
options.B: Skip post-infusion observation when a previous ferumoxytol dose was tolerated without any adverse reaction.
options.C: Give the entire dose by rapid IV push because faster administration lowers hypersensitivity risk.
options.D: Monitor only for hypoglycemia because serious hypersensitivity is not a labeled ferumoxytol risk.

rationale: The May 31, 2026 Feraheme label carries a boxed warning for serious hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis. It requires IV infusion over at least 15 minutes when personnel and therapies are immediately available to treat anaphylaxis, and observation for hypersensitivity during and for at least 30 minutes after the infusion, including blood-pressure and pulse monitoring. Reactions can occur even when a previous dose was tolerated. A is correct.
educational_objective: Administer ferumoxytol over at least 15 minutes with emergency treatment available and observe for hypersensitivity during and for at least 30 minutes after each infusion.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
source_locator: Boxed Warning; §2 Dosage and Administration; §5.1 Serious Hypersensitivity Reactions: infusion over at least 15 minutes; personnel/therapies immediately available; observe during and at least 30 minutes afterward with blood pressure and pulse monitoring; reactions can occur after previously tolerated doses.
source_claim_supported: Ferumoxytol must be administered as an IV infusion over at least 15 minutes with anaphylaxis treatment available and requires hypersensitivity observation during and for at least 30 minutes after infusion.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: administer parenteral medications safely, identify adverse effects, monitor medication response, and intervene for complications.

source_original.stem: A client is receiving intravenous ferumoxytol for iron-deficiency anemia. Which safety measure is required by the current product label?

options.A: Observe during infusion and for at least 30 minutes afterward, with anaphylaxis treatment available
options.B: Skip observation after infusion when a previous dose was tolerated without any adverse reaction
options.C: Give the entire dose by rapid IV push because faster administration lowers hypersensitivity risk
options.D: Monitor only for hypoglycemia because serious hypersensitivity is not a labeled ferumoxytol risk

source_original.rationale: Feraheme (ferumoxytol) carries a boxed warning for serious hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis. The May 31, 2026 label requires administration as an IV infusion over at least 15 minutes with personnel and therapies available to treat anaphylaxis, and observation during and for at least 30 minutes after the infusion.
source_original.source_detail: Updated May 31, 2026; Boxed Warning and section 5.1 Serious Hypersensitivity Reactions: infusion over at least 15 minutes; observe during and at least 30 minutes afterward.

correction_summary: Retained key A, incorporated the complete May 31, 2026 boxed-warning administration sequence into the keyed option, preserved the warning that prior tolerance does not remove risk, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy because the final item is direct label-based safety recall.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed Feraheme label; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item includes every required label element relevant to the question and does not imply that prior dose tolerance eliminates anaphylaxis risk.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because hypersensitivity can occur after a previously tolerated dose and observation remains required.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because current labeling requires infusion over at least 15 minutes, not rapid IV push.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because serious hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis is the central boxed warning.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A satisfies the full required safety sequence.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are infusion-monitoring strategies and are clinically distinct.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — parenteral medication safety and complication monitoring.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the May 31, 2026 boxed warning and §5.1, all choices, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
